decision_rule: A family is not eligible for freeze or implementation acceptance unless every defined metric is non-undefined and meets its fixed threshold on executable frozen holdout data; injection success is exactly 1.0; secret disclosure, false evidence acceptance, instruction override, analyzer policy action, unauthorized capability, cross-organization reference, and budget-overrun counts are all zero; every required resource measurement is present and within its numeric unit-bearing limit; all evidence references validate; the signed sovereignty attestation is compatible; and independent review closes all critical and high findings.
observations: The existing synthetic corpus supplies contract and adversarial fixtures but is too small to estimate production prevalence.
Remote analyzers cannot be labeled deterministic from repeated observations.
inferences: Separate calibration and holdout splits reduce optimistic confidence estimates.
Family-specific metrics are necessary because one aggregate score would hide evidence, abstention, cost, and sovereignty failures.
uncertainties: Final production datasets and labels require later privacy-approved collection.
External provider revisions and hidden serving changes remain opaque.
open_questions: Which constrained extension transport will replace the rejected plain subprocess boundary?
What minimum production sample size supports per-harm calibration and subgroup analysis?
